evidence.title: OpenHands Persistent memory; MCP health; Per-backend settings
evidence.locator: Persistent memory; MCP health; Per-backend settings
evidence.finding: Canvas loads workspace/user persistent memory when enabled. Skills/MCP/secrets are backend-scoped. MCP health distinguishes reachable, rejected credentials and connection failure; public-server reachability does not verify credentials. Skills load on new conversation start.

evidence.locator: Run statuses; Activity costs; Shared automation conversations; Export/import

evidence.finding: Canvas documents phone/tablet browser access through Tailscale or authenticated public-mode ngrok; it does not establish native mobile apps.

evidence.title: OpenHands Roles table; Private settings
evidence.finding: Cloud/Enterprise organization roles are Member, Admin and Owner. Members create conversations and own private MCP/secrets/settings; Admins invite/promote users and manage LLM settings/credits; Owners delete organizations and claim Git organizations. Private settings remain private from other members including admins.

evidence.title: OpenHands Plan cards; Comparison table
evidence.finding: Canvas is free, MIT, single-user/shared-identity and self-hosted. Teams is $500 monthly for up to ten users with $50 monthly per additional seat, 5000 sessions per month, 30-day trial, RBAC and SSO/SAML. Enterprise has custom pricing. LLM keys are user-provided.

evidence.title: OpenHands Enterprise managed gateway budgets; Usage; Why totals differ
evidence.locator: Enterprise managed gateway budgets; Usage; Why totals differ
evidence.finding: Enterprise managed-gateway budgets cap organization/user monthly spend. Gateway admits requests and can block at limits; direct provider calls are outside enforcement. evidence.title: OpenHands docs/ACP_AGENTS.md
evidence.finding: Local ACP agents reuse provider-native logins; clean containers/cloud need credentials. Pi/OpenCode are offered only on local/self-hosted backends. Agent choice is per backend and running conversations retain their original agent.

evidence.locator: src/routes/app-settings.tsx lines 112-136 and 217-231 (enable-analytics-switch), release v1.38.0 commit e14b76c
evidence.finding: App settings render a 'send anonymous usage data' switch that defaults on and saves user_consents_to_analytics and the telemetry consent as granted or denied. On a Cloud backend the switch is disabled and stays on.

evidence.title: Agent Canvas telemetry consent modal
evidence.finding: A telemetry consent modal asks the user whether to send anonymous usage data and saves the choice as granted or denied.

evidence.title: OpenHands Enterprise SAML SSO guide
evidence.finding: The guide explains how to let users of an OpenHands Enterprise installation sign in through a corporate SAML identity provider such as Okta, Entra ID, Google Workspace or ADFS.

evidence.title: OpenHands pricing
evidence.locator: Plan cards and comparison table (Agent Canvas, Teams, Enterprise)
evidence.finding: Agent Canvas is free and MIT licensed. Teams costs 500 USD per month for up to ten users plus 50 USD per extra seat and lists SSO/SAML and RBAC; Enterprise has custom pricing. The page returns HTTP 403 to some automated fetchers but loads with a browser user agent.

evidence.title: OpenHands native mobile MVP
evidence.finding: The public native Expo MVP can list conversations, stream history/events and send messages to a reachable Agent Server using a session API key. Source-build instructions cover Android and iOS with native toolchains. Cloud login, QR pairing and a laptop remote-session facade are still planned; no store/release binary is asserted.

evidence.title: OpenHands native mobile Agent Server client
evidence.finding: The native mobile client implements REST conversation listing/history and sends message events to /api/conversations/{id}/events; ChatScreen calls that sendMessage path, and useConversationSocket streams events through WebSocket. app.json declares iOS and Android native platforms.

evidence.title: Agent Canvas command-line launcher
evidence.locator: CLI entry point; help/info; local stack startup
evidence.finding: The product-owned agent-canvas CLI starts the local Agent Server, automation backend and pre-built frontend. It exposes version, stack-info, public/frontend-only/backend-only and help flags. This establishes a user-runnable launcher CLI, without asserting a separate task-operation CLI.

evidence.title: Canvas conversation task list
evidence.finding: The Canvas Task List derives its entries from the latest TaskTrackerObservation in the current conversation event store. IDs are generated from list position and statuses are todo/in_progress/done. Inspection of the native task-list route and API/store surfaces found no independent issue/backlog work-item entity; automations are separate trigger definitions.

evidence.title: OpenHands current self-hosted plan table
evidence.locator: Agent Canvas, Teams and Enterprise; Comparison table
evidence.finding: The current public price table lists free self-hosted Canvas, self-hosted Teams at $500/month for ten users plus $50/month additional seats, capped at 5000 sessions monthly, and custom Enterprise. It lists no one-time licence. The separately linked Cloud backend is not priced in this table.

evidence.title: OpenHands Cloud model credits
evidence.finding: Cloud users must buy at least $10 in credits before generating an OpenHands LLM Key. That key can be used in the CLI, self-hosted OpenHands or other coding agents. These are model-provider credits, not proof of a metered ADE or sandbox price.
